messages:
jess: FYI getting spike in EU p95/p99 for /v1/generate reported by AcmeCorp ~started 10:02 UTC. They say p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~700-900ms, p99 ~1.2s. No errors, just high latency. customer-provided curl below. can oncall grab traces?

samir: oncall here. grabbing traces now. do we have a customer request id?

jess: they included request-id `req_0a1b2c3d` and sample: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer ...\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"test"}' -v`

ops-bot: New alert: EU-EDGE TLS handshake p95 increased by 550ms in last 30m. Link: https://internal.metrics/redwood/alerts/5392 :rotating_light:

samir: looking at edge access logs for region=eu-west-1 around 1769854320..1769854600. Observed a cluster of connections with initial connection time ~600ms (TLS handshake time). Backend processing stable.

kai: I pulled a tcpdump from edge-pop-eu-west-1-03 for one sample client IP. Here's trimmed output:```
15:02:10.123 IP client > edge: SYN
15:02:10.124 IP edge > client: SYN,ACK
15:02:10.712 IP client > edge: ACK  # RTT ~589ms
15:02:10.712 TLS ClientHello
15:02:11.300 TLS ServerHello # handshake ~588-700ms
```
Noticed large gap before Client ACK completing TCP handshake. smells like cross-AZ routing causing extra hops.

dina: we saw a change in BGP path churn reported by our peering provider at 15:01 UTC (spike in route flaps). Might align. pinging peering contacts.

eli: customer latency timeline matches our metric spike. No deploys in the timeframe. Any DNS changes?

kai: checked DNS: TTLs stable at 60s, and resolving to our anycast IPs as expected. However traceroute from a sampled client shows traffic leaving eu-west-1 and bouncing to eu-central-1 PoP before returning:```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (52.17.x.y), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.5 ms 0.3 ms 0.4 ms
 6  xi-popeu-west  12 ms 14 ms 13 ms
 7  transit-ix  18 ms 20 ms 19 ms
 8  popeu-central-1  85 ms 88 ms 86 ms  # unexpected cross-pop hop
 9  edge-back  90 ms 89 ms 91 ms
```
That extra detour adds ~70ms roundtrip, but handshake gaps show ~500-700ms — something else adding delay.

samir: looking at TLS metrics, the server-side handshake time has two components: TCP connect + TLS. Most affected requests show long time between SYN-ACK and first TLS bytes. That indicates client delay in sending ClientHello or network reordering. Could be path MTU or packet loss causing retransmit. packet capture shows retransmits from client side.

jess: customer says their clients are in Frankfurt and hit our EU endpoint. They also note intermittent higher loss on their side (they're a CDN provider).

kai: queued an AWS support ticket (if this is helpful) and opened peering ticket with our ISP. In parallel, we can try steering traffic to a different anycast edge or pin customers to local PoP via DNS weight change. Thoughts?

eli: quick mitigation: reduce DNS TTL for the impacted zone and shift weight away from the suspect PoP (eu-central-1). For long term we'll need route stability from transit.

dina: I can push a temporary traffic steering change in edge-control: set preference tag `prefer_region=eu-west` for AcmeCorp prefix and lower TTL to 10s. That will force new lookups to prefer eu-west-only anycast IPs. Ready to deploy if SRE approves.

samir: go for it. coordinate with kai to monitor for collateral impact.

kai: doing change now:```
# edge-control CLI
edge-control traffic-set --customer acmecorp --prefer-region eu-west --dns-ttl 10 --dry-run=false
```
applied at 15:13 UTC.

ops-bot: Config change applied by kai at 1769854397.

samir: immediate metric check: p95 dropped from ~720ms -> ~150ms over next 45s. p99 trending down too. Nice.

jess: customer confirmed improvement on their side, p95 now ~140ms. They said they saw routing change within 30s. :tada:

kai: follow-ups: 1) keep DNS ttl=60 after vendor confirms peering stable, 2) get BGP flap root cause from ISP, 3) add session-ticket/session-resumption debug to edge to reduce full-handshake incidence for future transient reroutes.

dina: opened NET-452 (internal) to track long-term work: vendor RCA, BGP filters, anycast health metrics. Assigned to kai.

eli: can product / customer success reach back to AcmeCorp with summary? I can draft.

jess: yes please. also note: mitigation was traffic steering at edge-control, not a code change.

samir: closing loop here — marking incident as mitigated. leaving thread open for NET-452 follow-up.

nick: (from AcmeCorp) Thanks team — performance is back to normal. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

ops-bot: Incident: mitigated at 1769854490. Follow-up ticket NET-452 created.

samir: adding one final note — we should consider adding an automated fallback that pins by-region for sessions that see repeated TLS full-handshakes >3x in a short window. That would avoid repeated cross-pop rehandshakes during transient routing issues.

kai: agreed. I'll add to NET-452 backlog.
